name: Vantablack Media Hollow Tongue Relay
description: The Hollow Tongue Relay is a passive dead-drop infrastructure device disguised as an ordinary piece of urban furniture or commercial detritus — a cracked utility panel, a branded vending machine fascia, a municipal drainage marker. Internally it houses a heavily shielded, ultra-low-power mesh node that stores encrypted message packets in a write-once buffer, broadcasting nothing until a specifically keyed query device passes within two meters and triggers a silent, microsecond burst transmission. The relay never initiates contact and emits no continuous signal, making it invisible to both passive monitoring grids and active sweep protocols.

specifications.detectability: No continuous emission; burst detectable only within 0.5m with specialized hardware
specifications.query_device: Dedicated keyed fob or compatible implant
specifications.form_factor: Variable; disguised as environmental object, 8–30cm housing

tactical_use: Hollow Tongue Relays are placed along established courier routes, safe house approaches, and contested territory boundaries. Operatives pass by without stopping, pulling queued messages with a hand-in-pocket fob sweep that takes under a second. The absence of any meeting, any call, any digital handshake means there is nothing for surveillance networks to flag. Messages can be left by any authorized party, creating asynchronous communication chains that survive the loss or capture of individual nodes.
cultural_context: Vantablack Media's involvement in dead-drop infrastructure is an open secret in GLMZ — the company publicly manufactures urban signage and environmental media installations, providing perfect cover for deploying relays city-wide under municipal contracts. Street networks, resistance cells, and competing corporate factions all use the same underlying hardware, creating a strange shared infrastructure of secrets. Finding an unkeyed relay and cracking its buffer is considered a significant intelligence coup; the black market for harvested relay data is substantial.
story_hooks: The players discover a Hollow Tongue Relay that appears to be double-keyed — someone has been reading the same dead drop as their contact, and has been leaving counter-messages designed to look like the original sender.
A relay placed by a now-dead resistance leader still contains unread messages that predate the cell's destruction; the contents could expose who betrayed them.
Vantablack Media wins a city contract to install 'smart urban signage' across a district the players operate in — within weeks, their operational security begins inexplicably degrading.
A relay's camouflage housing is so convincing it was accidentally incorporated into a building renovation; the construction crew is now unknowingly carrying it in a sealed wall.
related_entities: MindBridge Relay One Social Integration BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately nondescript urban fixture designed to be visually ignored—weathered utility panel, damaged transit shelter panel, or cracked municipal infrastructure signage. The exterior mimics years of neglect with authentic-looking corrosion, graffiti patches, and UV degradation. No visible electronics or antenna arrays. Resembles discarded urban detritus rather than functional hardware.
physical_description.dimensions: 8–30cm housing depending on disguise form factor; most commonly 20×15×4cm (utility panel variant)
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight, handheld or wall-mountable; 300–800g depending on housing material and internal shielding mass
physical_description.primary_material: Exterior: fiber-reinforced polymer or corroded steel cladding (cosmetic). Interior: 3mm mu-metal Faraday cage with composite RF shielding; dense tungsten-lead layer for signal isolation
physical_description.finish: Deliberately weathered and degraded—faded paint, rust bloom patterns, mock water stains, authentic scuff marks and scratches. Some variants feature printed graffiti tags or municipal stickers to enhance camouflage. Non-reflective matte surface throughout
physical_description.color_scheme: Drab utility palette: muted grays, browns, faded industrial greens, corroded copper tones. Accent layers in weathered blues or yellow warning stripe fragments. All colors intentionally desaturated and aged-looking
physical_description.interface_elements: Virtually none visible externally. Disguise authenticity includes fake panel rivets, mock bolt heads, printed warning labels. Internal access point (hidden beneath cosmetic layer) features recessed 2mm diagnostic port and orientation marker visible only to operator. No LEDs, displays, or indicators; all status confirmation silent and electromagnetic
distinctive_features: Authentically mimicked environmental decay—micro-texturing replicates real corrosion and weathering
Zero visible antenna or transmission hardware; RF harvesting grid embedded in shielding layers
Internal burst transmitter frequency-locked to keyed query device only; cross-talk rejection rated to −180dB
Thermal signature matches ambient within 0.3°C due to passive RF harvesting (no active heating)
Cosmetic damage patterns randomized during manufacture to prevent serial recognition
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Vantablack Media brand mark laser-etched into internal mu-metal shield (invisible without disassembly). No external manufacturer identification; deliberately absent to maintain camouflage. Regulatory compliance marks printed on internal cavity only. Unit serial encoded in burst transmission metadata only
physical_description.condition_typical: Appears abandoned and non-functional in situ. May accumulate real dust, debris, or environmental weathering during deployment. No maintenance indicators or status lights. Operator must physically approach within 2m with keyed fob to confirm operational status via silent microsecond handshake
